headline: New Zealand Delivers Tightest Election in Years as Voters Desert Major Parties
summary: New Zealand voters delivered the country's tightest election in years amid a low national mood and declining faith in politics. Voters deserted the major political parties at the polls.
why: New Zealand general elections determine the composition of parliament and government leadership, shaping fiscal, economic, and regulatory policies. Shifts in government leadership can influence national economic direction and domestic market sentiment.
